newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy meets Albanian rebels in bid to foster deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy meets Albanian rebels in bid to foster deal.

text.p: Italy met leaders of southern Albania's uprising on Monday on a warship in the Adriatic in a bid to foster a dialogue between the rebels and the authorities in Tirana, the Italian Foreign Ministry said.

A ministry statement said the talks were taking place on the amphibious assault ship San Giorgio between Italy's ambassador to Albania, Paolo Foresti, and rebel representatives from the port of Vlore and other southern Albanian towns.

The meeting was organised a day after Albanian President Sali Berisha, his ruling Democratic Party and nine opposition parties signed an agreement aimed at securing a political solution to the armed uprising in the south of the Balkan state.

The accord provides for an all-party government and new elections by June under international supervision. It gives rebels a week to hand in their weapons and asks parliament to declare an amnesty for all those implicated in the revolt.
The rebels, now in control of most of southern Albania after a week of insurrection, have given no sign that they intend to lay down their arms.
A spokesman for the uprising in the major town of Berat, which the army abandoned without a fight on Sunday, said rebels supported the idea of a caretaker government.
But they insisted on the resignation of Berisha, whom they blamed for allowing pyramid investment schemes to flourish before collapsing with the savings of hundreds of thousands.

Monday's Italian statement said "the authorities in Tirana have asked the Italian government's cooperation in initiating a dialogue with representatives of the movements operating in Vlore and other towns in the south" of Albania.
The request had been made "in order to consolidate and hasten" implementation of the Tirana agreement, it said.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini visited Tirana on Sunday night shortly after the deal was signed. He said after meeting Berisha and the opposition that Italy had been asked to underwrite the accord and monitor its application.

Monday's statement said the rebel representatives, ferried to the San Giorgio by helicopter, had been told by Foresti that Italy was ready to supply humanitarian aid and, with the European Union, help to revive Albania's shattered economy.
Diplomatic sources said no Albanian government representatives were at the shipboard meeting with the rebels.
"Foresti is likely to try to convince them that the accord was made in good faith and is a serious agreement. He will try to convince them to talk to Tirana," one source said.
Italy, which briefly occupied Albania under Fascism in World War Two, has strong cultural and commercial links with the tiny Balkan state, Europe's poorest country.
It has been active in seeking a peaceful solution to the unrest and has bolstered its military presence in the Adriatic out of fear that all-out war in Albania could trigger an exodus of refugees.

Italy has evacuated 78 foreigners from Vlore in the past week in three rescue missions using military helicopters. The latest airlift on Monday brought out six Italians, two Albanians, a German and an American, the foreign ministry said.
